issues.claim: Persists at its second end. §7.7 item 12's key cell (l. 12119), fixed this round per R4-15 (c), keeps a key minted at creation 'for the document's life (a later readable `id` neither replaces it nor is checked against it)', and V08 §2.4's `id` row (l. 634) says the same. §14 states `E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT` twice: the `PortResult` comment (l. 19600, 'an absorb whose digest's settlement key differs from the binding's — never for an offer whose `id` fell back (V08 §2.4)') and the absorb paragraph (l. 19722). The exception covers only an offer whose own `id` fell back. Take a map created from an id-less dossier (`settlement:map:<mapId>`) that later absorbs the same dossier now carrying a readable `id`. The offer's `id` did not fall back, and its digest's key `settlement:<id>` differs from the binding's, so §14 refuses it; §7.7 item 12 and V08 absorb it. Two units state two outcomes for one case (R3-03 (b)). Round 3's second end, which R4-15 (c) took verbatim, named only the offer's fallback.
issues.required_change: §14 l. 19600: 'never for an offer whose `id` fell back (V08 §2.4)' → 'never for an offer whose `id` fell back, nor against a settlement key minted at the document's creation (`settlement:map:<mapId>`), which a later readable `id` is not checked against (§7.7 item 12; V08 §2.4)'. §14 l. 19722: '(never for an offer whose `id` fell back, V08 §2.4)' → '(never for an offer whose `id` fell back, nor against a key minted at the document's creation, which a later readable `id` is not checked against; §7.7 item 12, V08 §2.4)'.

issues.claim: §6.3 *Plan damage* (l. 9969–9973), the comparison's home, says each element 'shows damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t', with only the roofless case excepted. R4-03's END lines this round added a second case. V03 §5.6 (2) (a) (V03 l. 2692–2694) reads 'an element is compared with the level only from its entry week ((b); V06 §3.23 (3))'. V06 §3.23 (3) (l. 3436–3442) makes an element a restoring event's re-cut mints enter the damage only at the week that restoration ends, 'Before that week it is drawn as built'. §2.6 step 7 (l. 2099–2101) agrees. So during a `reoccupy` whose `repair` Works still runs, a minted partition whose t the level still reaches is drawn damaged by §6.3's 'exactly' and drawn as built by V03, V06 and §2.6. Two outcomes for one case: the class R4-14 graded major for VDC3-02, and R4-03's sweep did not list §6.3. The same paragraph also concludes 'so a building never decayed draws its plan unchanged', while §2.6 step 7, §8.6 and V03 §5.6 (2) (a) ('never decayed and under no look') draw it damaged under a disaster look.
issues.required_change: §6.3 *Plan damage*: 'the element shows damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t — but for §2.6 step 7's one case without a threshold' → 'the element shows damaged exactly while the level is above 0 and at least t, compared only from its entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (b); for an element a restoring event's re-cut mints, the week that restoration ends, before which it draws as built, V06 §3.23 (3)) — but for §2.6 step 7's one case without a threshold'; and 'A level of 0 damages nothing else, so a building never decayed draws its plan unchanged (`item123.damage`)' → 'A level of 0 damages nothing else, so a building never decayed and under no disaster look (§2.6 step 7) draws its plan unchanged (`item123.damage`)'.

issues.claim: This round §6.1 *The weather stream* (l. 9561–9564) makes a press while a spell is in force wait until that spell's strength falls 'to 0 at its kind's fade rate (§8.4 (i))'; only then does the pressed spell start. §8.4 (i) (l. 13829–13830), the fades' home, states only 'at least 5 s for a shower, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze and cloud cover, V11's rows never shorter'. It gives nothing for `snow`, `leaves` or `shimmer`, and only a lower bound for the rest. V11's rows hold no fade field (`ClimateSettings.weather.kinds` carries `lengthS` and `hours` only). So a press during a snow spell has no defined wait, though snow falls 3 an hour through a temperate winter. When the pressed spell starts is then undefined, and so is T124-9's replay of that case. §8.4 (i)'s own phase, V11 §3.25.11's rule (every `lengthS` lower end 'at least twice its kind's fade in §8.4 (i)') and T-V11-48 (c) also read a fade for every kind. Two builders would give snow different fades and start the pressed spell at different times.
issues.required_change: §8.4 (i): 'its strength s in [0, 1] by its phase (rising from 0 and back to 0 over its fades: at least 5 s for a shower, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze and cloud cover, V11's rows never shorter)' → 'its strength s in [0, 1] by its phase (rising from 0 and back to 0, each over its kind's fade: 5 s for a shower (`rain`, `drizzle`), `snow` and `leaves`, 60 s for fog, mist, dust haze, cloud cover and heat shimmer — each kind's `lengthS` lower end in V11 §3.25.11 at least twice it; §6.1's press reads the same fade)'. Every V11 row and override already meets twice these fades: rain 30, drizzle 60, snow 60, leaves 20, mist 120, cloudShadow 120, shimmer 120, dust 120, fog 180 s; arid rain 20–60 s.

issues.claim: §7.1's new `bend.raised.underSpan` row (l. 10594) sends a ground `drawWay`, a moved way or a carve 'to cross under the nearest `open` span that holds it'. It gives no outcome where no `open` span of the raised way holds it: every span `vault`, or none of the clear width (the way's width + `clearWidthM`) or soffit §4.3 (l. 5627–5629) requires. A `primary` street drawn across a timber elevated road whose open spans are narrower than its corridor is an ordinary hand edit that meets this. The catch-all row's cause is 'every other infeasible declaration', so it excludes the case this row names. §4.3 gives generation's routes an else rung ('else the route takes another course by F-ROUTE's ladder'); the hand case has none, so builders would refuse, route round, or leave the crossing. The repair seat flagged this as a hand-off.
issues.required_change: §7.1's `bend.raised.underSpan` row, third cell: 'the way or channel moved to cross under the nearest `open` span that holds it, named in one line' → 'the way or channel moved to cross under the nearest `open` span that holds it; where no `open` span of the raised way holds it (every span `vault`, or none of the clear width or soffit §4.3 requires), a way takes another course by F-ROUTE's ladder as a route re-solve does (§4.3; §5.2) — round the raised way's feet, else the ladder's last rung (`unserved`, reported) — and a carve's channel stops at the edges of the under-deck strip, ending against the ground as against a berm (§2.7's support step (6) (a)), reported; named in one line'. (Second end for the adjudicator: T-V9-52 or T110-2's clause (5) adds 'a road wider than every `open` span's clear width drawn across a viaduct: routed round its feet, with `bend.raised.underSpan`'.)

issues.claim: §2.7's support step (3) (l. 2552–2556) holds the band's stretch under a crossing station while the deck stands: 'no writer of its condition but a landfall leaves it `breached` or `dismantled`'. The station's support is that stretch, and its `supports` entry 'reads its stretch's `condition`'. This round §7.1 gained `bend.wall.held` (l. 10592) for a hand `convert` `breach` or `dismantle` only. A `delete` of the enceinte, or of the raised gate or wall opening there, is no condition write, and §7.1 *Delete* (l. 10469–10476) and the outcome table give it no rule. V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1605–1612; J-V6.114, J-V6.140) keeps such a stretch through `wallToWay` and `absorbWall` as a free-standing arch or gate tower. Read literally, a hand delete of a town wall that an aqueduct passes by its arch removes the deck's support: the deck is left on a station with no ring, and a `supports` entry reads a stretch that no longer exists, an impossible structure. A builder might refuse instead. The outcome is undefined on an ordinary CITY edit.
issues.required_change: §7.1's `bend.wall.held` row, cause cell: 'a hand `convert` `breach` or `dismantle` of an enceinte stretch meeting the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands (§2.7's support step (3))' → 'a hand `convert` `breach` or `dismantle` of an enceinte stretch, or a `delete` of the enceinte or of its raised gate or wall opening there, meeting the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands (§2.7's support step (3))'. Outcome cell, after 'an op wholly on the held stretch changes nothing, with its line', add '; a `delete` takes the rest and leaves the held stretch standing as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, as `wallToWay` and `absorbWall` leave it (V06 §3.7.6 (5)), the enceinte's record kept while such a stretch stands'. (Second end for the adjudicator: T-V9-52 adds 'a wall deleted while a viaduct's deck stands on its raised gate: the gate tower kept, carrying the deck, with `bend.wall.held`'.)

issues.claim: §4.11's `wallToWay(enceinte)` (l. 8189–8196), the operator's home for epochs and hand converts alike, ends 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option'. V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1605–1612; J-V6.114, J-V6.140) says '`absorbWall` and `wallToWay` leave standing every raised way that crosses the old line; the new ring road takes no junction with it: its opening or raised gate in the old curtain stays as a free-standing arch or gate tower'. §4.8 (l. 7643–7650) makes that raised gate 'a gate whose tower carries the deck'. A builder of §4.11's operator removes the tower that carries a standing viaduct's deck and makes its gate a junction; the evolution builder keeps both. Two units state two outcomes for one case (R3-03 (b)), and §4.11's reading leaves a deck without its support.
issues.required_change: §4.11 *`wallToWay(enceinte)`*: 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option.' → 'towers are removed; gates become junctions with a `square` option — save the stretch held under a raised way's crossing station while its deck stands (a raised gate with its tower, the curtain under an aqueduct's arch), which stays as a free-standing gate tower or arch carrying the deck, the new ring road taking no junction with the raised way (§2.7's support step (3); V06 §3.7.6 (5)).'

issues.claim: This round §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10593) takes 'a hand `drawWall` … across a standing raised way', and an aqueduct is a raised way. §13.2's T110-2 (4) (l. 18414–18418) requires 'a hand `drawWall` across a standing aqueduct … the hand case naming `bend.wall.raisedCrossing`'. V09 §4.20.2 (4) (l. 3005–3007) still gives that case `bend.wall.aqueductArch` ('From the other side, a wall T3 `wall` draws across a standing aqueduct shows an arch in its ghost, not a gate (`bend.wall.aqueductArch`)'), then names `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` for the same crossing two sentences later. §7.1's catch-all still lists 'a wall's … aqueduct arch'. One case, two keys. The geometry is the same; the dry run's line differs (an id).
issues.required_change: V09 §4.20.2 (4): 'An aqueduct passes through an arch in the curtain, never a gate (item 110 (b)), and its ghost draws the arch mark.' → 'An aqueduct drawn across a standing wall passes through an arch in the curtain, never a gate (item 110 (b)), and its ghost draws the arch mark (`bend.wall.aqueductArch`).'; 'From the other side, a wall T3 `wall` draws across a standing aqueduct shows an arch in its ghost, not a gate (`bend.wall.aqueductArch`).' → 'From the other side, a wall T3 `wall` draws across a standing aqueduct shows an arch in its ghost, not a gate — the crossing below (`bend.wall.raisedCrossing`; T110-2).'. V09 §4.9's `bend.wall.aqueductArch` row, source cell 'file f item 363' → 'file f item 363: an aqueduct drawn across a standing wall (§7.1's *Raised ways, aqueducts and retaining walls*)'. (Second end, determinism: §7.1's catch-all 'a wall's ridge, reach, waterfront, open ground and aqueduct arch' → 'a wall's ridge, reach, waterfront and open ground, the arch a wall takes for an aqueduct drawn across it'.)

issues.claim: This round's press rule makes a pressed spell wait while the running one fades out, and 'a further press before then changes nothing' (§6.1 l. 9564; V09 §4.21.14 (4)). V09 §4.21.14 (1) keeps **Start a shower now** 'enabled while the effects are on and a weather kind is live'. So for up to a minute the button is enabled and a press does nothing visible: the silent no-op §7.8 forbids ('disabled with its reason row — never a silent no-op'). §6.1 and V09 (4) already apply that rule to the moment with no live kind. Row 93 and T-V9-87 test 'nothing changed by the second press'. The repair seat flagged this as a hand-off.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.14 (1): 'enabled while the effects are on and a weather kind is live ((4))' → 'enabled while the effects are on, a weather kind is live and no pressed spell waits ((4))'. (4): 'a further press before then changes nothing (§6.1 *The weather stream*)' → 'until then the button is disabled with `settings.weather.coming` ("Your shower is on its way."), never a silent no-op (§7.8), so no further press is made (§6.1 *The weather stream*)'. V09 §4.9 adds the `settings.weather.coming` row. Row 93's 'nothing changed by the second press' and T-V9-87's 'a second press before then changes nothing' → 'the button disabled with `settings.weather.coming` until the pressed spell starts'.
